artboards.title: A — One thing at a time

annotations.text:
CHOSEN 31 Aug — the shop is the progress bar.

There is no step counter and no progress strip. The merchant's own shop sits at the top, and it fills in as they answer: the sign goes up as they type, the whole shop restyles as they swipe a look, their product lands on the shelf as they name it. Nothing about where you are needs reading.

Four steps: name and money, look, first product, open.

Every colour and heading font is the real one, read out of ThemeResolver. Prices are sample values.

TWO THINGS CHANGED SINCE THE PICK

1 · Money is now asked. C skipped it — the preview showed GH₵ the merchant never chose, and a store cannot be created without a currency. It sits under the shop name on step 1, and picking it re-prices the shop above you.

2 · The shop is dressed from the first screen. C used to open on an empty grey box, which was its weakest moment. It now opens wearing the default Market look with only the sign and the shelf unfinished — so it reads as a real shop waiting for its name, and swiping a look still visibly transforms it.

STILL OPEN

· Photo upload is drawn but not wired — the shelf fills from the product name and price only.

· Currency shows as GH₵ / ₦ / $, replacing the flag emoji the live page ships today.

· The buyer-protection question keeps the wording that is live now: asked, never defaulted on.

· Nothing here is built in Elixir yet. This is the design, not a branch.

Parked, kept for the record.

TODAY — the page that ships now, at phone width. Progress is four identical grey bars and the words "Step 2 of 4"; 22 themes in eleven rows of two, each explained by a line of text.

A — ONE THING AT A TIME. One question per screen; asks what you sell first, then shows four looks for that trade. Cost: six screens instead of four. Still the best answer if the 22-theme grid ever needs to shrink further.

B — THE ROAD. Four stops on a parcel-tracking road, the same tracker the dashboard setup strip uses. Cost: 150px of every screen, and it repeats a metaphor the merchant meets again on the dashboard.

Both are still clickable.
